questions.question: On simple interest, a certain sum of money amounts to ₹1,400 in 2 years and to ₹2,000 in 5 years. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Amount** = Interest for the difference in **Time**.

Interest for (5 − 2) = 3 years → ₹2,000 − ₹1,400 = ₹600.

Interest for 1 year = ₹200. ⇒ Interest for 2 years = ₹400.

**Principal (P)** = Amount₂yᵣ − SI₂yᵣ = 1,400 − 400 = ₹1,000.

Rate % = (Interest₁yᵣ ÷ P) × 100 = (200 ÷ 1,000) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6bf99ba6a9ba7bc35e9dcf3a3edc79972437bcf7641237f7fd007b61edb62de6.png] 

**Given:** Amount in 2 years (A₁) = ₹1,400, Amount in 5 years (A₂) = ₹2,000.

**Formula:** Amount = Principal + (P × R × T ÷ 100)

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** for 3 years = A₂ − A₁ = 2,000 − 1,400 = ₹600.

⇒ SI for 1 year = 600 ÷ 3 = ₹200.

⇒ SI for 2 years = 200 × 2 = ₹400.

⇒ **Principal (P)** = Amount after 2 years − SI for 2 years = 1,400 − 400 = ₹1,000.

⇒ Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T) = (400 × 100) ÷ (1,000 × 2)

⇒ R = 40,000 ÷ 2,000 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Constant Property

In SI, the **interest earned** remains the same every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Effective Rate of Interest

Rate of Interest = (SI for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100. This is the fastest way to find **R** once P is known.

Difference between SI and CI

For the first year (if compounded annually), SI and CI are **equal**. From the second year, CI > SI.

a. Phloem helps in mineral and water absorption from the soil.

b. Root hair increases the root's surface area for water and mineral absorption.

c. Special vascular tissue in plants transports water and nutrients from the soil.

__
 
• **Phloem** is primarily responsible for the transport of sugars and other metabolic products downward from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• **Xylem** is the vascular tissue that is responsible for the transport of water and dissolved minerals absorbed from the soil.

• **Xylem Transport:**
 
 
• Xylem is composed of tracheids, vessel elements, fibers, and xylem parenchyma.
 
• It facilitates the upward movement of water and minerals through capillary action, root pressure, and transpiration pull.
 
 
 
• **Root Hair Function:**
 
 
• Root hairs are extensions of root epidermal cells that greatly increase the root surface area for water and nutrient uptake.
 
• They play a crucial role in the absorption of minerals and water from the soil.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Tissues:**
 
 
• Xylem and phloem are the two main types of vascular tissues in plants.

questions.question: If x : 6 :: 6 : y, then the value of sqrt{xy} is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any **continued proportion** a : b :: b : c, the property is b² = ac.

Here, x : 6 :: 6 : y ⇒ 6² = xy.

Taking square root on both sides: √xy = √(6²) = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x : 6 :: 6 : y

**Formula Used:** Product of Extremes = Product of Means

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6cab95df1b8e5d6263fb9c3a8582c37e59febd1e497369644b44563f9e14125.png] 

⇒ x/6 = 6/y

⇒ x × y = 6 × 6

⇒ xy = 36

⇒ √xy = √36

⇒ √xy = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(ab). In the given question, 6 is the mean proportional of x and y.

Third Proportional

If a : b :: b : c, then c is called the third proportional to a and b, calculated as c = b²/a.

Fourth Proportional

If a : b :: c : d, then d is the fourth proportional, calculated as d = (b × c)/a.</p

questions.question: A man sold a shirt for ₹960, at a loss of 4%. He sold a sweater for ₹840 at a profit of 20%. Find his net profit or loss.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Cost Price (CP)** = (960 ÷ 0.96) + (840 ÷ 1.20) = 1000 + 700 = ₹1700.

Total **Selling Price (SP)** = 960 + 840 = ₹1800.

Since **SP > CP**, it is a **Profit**.

Net Profit = 1800 − 1700 = ₹100.

**∴ The correct answer is Profit, ₹100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → SPₛₕᵢᵣₜ = ₹960, Loss% = 4%; SPₛwₑₐₜₑᵣ = ₹840, Profit% = 20%.
Formulas: CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 ± Profit/Loss%]; Net Profit/Loss = Total SP − Total CP.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee764463b439b8383b380d7656a915867f660d2b64b8a5e691df74cbbe314a61.png] 
⇒ CP of Shirt = (960 × 100) ÷ (100 − 4) = 96000 ÷ 96 = **₹1000**.
⇒ CP of Sweater = (840 × 100) ÷ (100 + 20) = 84000 ÷ 120 = **₹700**.
⇒ Total CP = 1000 + 700 = **₹1700**.
⇒ Total SP = 960 + 840 = **₹1800**.
⇒ Net Profit = 1800 − 1700 = **₹100**.

**∴ The correct answer is Profit, ₹100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when **Selling Price** is greater than **Cost Price**. Profit = SP − CP.

Net Transaction

To find the **Net Profit or Loss** on multiple items, always calculate the **sum of individual Cost Prices** and compare it with the **sum of individual Selling Prices**.

questions.question: Which pair in the reactivity series represents the most and least reactive metal pairs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium and gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potassium is the most reactive metal in the reactivity series. It reacts explosively with water and even moisture in the air.
 
• Gold is one of the least reactive metals and does not tarnish or corrode easily, maintaining its luster over time.
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity to help predict their behavior in reactions.
 
• Potassium's high reactivity is due to its single electron in the outermost shell, which it loses easily to form positive ions.
 
• Gold's low reactivity is due to its full d-subshell and high ionization energy, making it less likely to participate in chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series, also known as the activity series, is a ranking of metals based on their reactivity from highest to lowest.
 
• It helps predict how metals will react with acids, water, and other compounds.
 
• Metals high in the series, like potassium, sodium, and calcium, react more vigorously than those lower down, like gold, platinum, and silver.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity of Alkali Metals**
 
 
• Alkali metals, such as potassium and sodium, are highly reactive due to their single valence electron.
 
• They tend to lose this electron easily, forming positive ions and engaging in reactions with water, oxygen, and halogens.
 
 
 
• **Gold's Chemical Properties**
 
 
• Gold is known for its resistance to corrosion and tarnish, making it highly valuable in jewelry and electronics.
 
• It is a noble metal, meaning it is resistant to reacting with most chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Reactivity Series**
 
 
• The reactivity series is used in metallurgy to extract metals from their ores.
 
• It is also used in predicting the outcomes of displacement reactions in chemistry.

questions.question: The greatest natural number, which exactly divides the product of any four consecutive natural numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The product of **n consecutive natural numbers** is always divisible by **n!** (n factorial).

For **four consecutive natural numbers**, the product is divisible by **4!**.

4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

To verify, take the smallest four consecutive natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4.

Product = 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Four consecutive natural numbers.

**Formula Used:** Product of n consecutive integers is divisible by n!.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9536b69e888234f8939a4713399de935d8b3cd90322b3aef7d772631cb18c6d7.png] 

⇒ Let the four consecutive numbers be n, (n+1), (n+2), and (n+3).

⇒ Smallest set of natural numbers = 1, 2, 3, 4.

⇒ Product = 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.

⇒ Second set of natural numbers = 2, 3, 4, 5.

⇒ Product = 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = 120.

⇒ HCF of 24 and 120 is 24.

⇒ Therefore, the greatest natural number that divides any such product is 24.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility of Consecutive Integers

The product of **r** consecutive integers is always divisible by **r!**. This is because the number of ways to choose r items from n is an integer: ⁿCᵣ = P/r!, so P must be divisible by r!.

Factorial Definition

n! (n factorial) is the product of all positive integers from 1 up to n. For example, 3! = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.

Natural Numbers

Natural numbers start from **1, 2, 3, ...**. If the question allowed for whole numbers (including 0), the product could be 0, which is divisible by any number.</p

questions.question: When an object of mass 'm' falls freely to the ground from a height 'h’, at what point is the object's kinetic energy maximum?

options.text: At one-fourth way through the fall.
At the start of the fall.
When it is about to hit the ground.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When it is about to hit the ground.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object falls freely under gravity, its **potential energy is converted to kinetic energy**.
 
• The kinetic energy of an object is given by the formula **KE = 0.5 * m * v²**, where 'm' is mass and 'v' is velocity.
 
• As the object falls, its velocity increases due to acceleration by gravity, leading to **an increase in kinetic energy**.
 
• The **maximum kinetic energy** is achieved **just before the object hits the ground**, as all potential energy has been converted to kinetic energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potential Energy (PE):**

 
 
• It is the energy possessed by an object due to its position or height above the ground.
 
• PE is calculated using the formula **PE = m * g * h**, where 'm' is mass, 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity, and 'h' is height.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• This law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.
 
• In the case of a falling object, potential energy is converted to kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):**
 
 
• It is the acceleration experienced by an object due to the gravitational pull of the Earth.
 
• The standard value of 'g' is approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• A condition in which the only force acting on an object is gravity, causing it to fall towards the Earth.
 
• During free fall, air resistance is considered negligible.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 42 and one of them exceeds the other by 18. Find the greater number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Greater number** = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2

**Smaller number** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2

⇒ Greater number = (42 + 18) ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Sum of two numbers** = 42

**Difference between numbers** = 18

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5706dd75d8eab579a6d53a3b4bc1bf096db47ca12323899f89fdb0ca334e7517.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **greater number** be x and the **smaller number** be y.

⇒ x + y = 42 --- (1)

⇒ x − y = 18 --- (2)

Adding equations (1) and (2):

⇒ (x + y) + (x − y) = 42 + 18

⇒ 2x = 60

⇒ x = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

questions.question:
Simplify the following expression: 

 (sin theta)/(1-cos theta)+(1-cos theta)/(sin theta)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put **θ = 90°** in the expression.

⇒ sin 90° = 1 and cos 90° = 0.

⇒ [1 / (1 − 0)] + [(1 − 0) / 1] = 1 + 1 = **2**.

Check options at θ = 90°: 2 cosec 90° = 2 × 1 = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cosec θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expression = [sin θ / (1 − cos θ)] + [(1 − cos θ) / sin θ]

**Formula Used:** sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | cosec θ = 1 / sin θ

⇒ Take **LCM** of denominators: sin θ (1 − cos θ)

⇒ Expression = [sin²θ + (1 − cos θ)²] / [sin θ(1 − cos θ)]

⇒ Expression = [sin²θ + 1 + cos²θ − 2 cos θ] / [sin θ(1 − cos θ)]

⇒ Expression = [(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 1 − 2 cos θ] / [sin θ(1 − cos θ)]

⇒ Expression = [1 + 1 − 2 cos θ] / [sin θ(1 − cos θ)]

⇒ Expression = [2 − 2 cos θ] / [sin θ(1 − cos θ)]

⇒ Expression = 2(1 − cos θ) / [sin θ(1 − cos θ)]

⇒ Expression = 2 / sin θ

⇒ Expression = 2 cosec θ

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cosec θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Value Substitution Method

For simplification questions, substituting standard angles like 30°, 45°, or 60° helps in verifying options quickly, provided no denominator becomes zero.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a prime number?
questions.solution:

Check the **divisibility** of each number by small **prime numbers** like 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

**Given:** Numbers 61, 91, 71, 31.

⇒ Factors of 61 = 1, 61 (**Prime**)

⇒ Factors of 71 = 1, 71 (**Prime**)

⇒ Factors of 31 = 1, 31 (**Prime**)

⇒ Factors of 91 = 1, 7, 13, 91

⇒ Since 91 has **factors** other than 1 and 91, it is a **composite number**.

**∴ The correct answer is 91.**

**__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers 1-100

There are 25 prime numbers between 1 and 100. 2 is the only **even prime number**.

Composite Numbers

Numbers that have more than two factors. 1 is neither **prime** nor **composite**.

Divisibility Rule of 7

Double the last digit and subtract it from the rest of the number. If the result is divisible by 7, the original number is divisible by 7.</p

questions.question: In a parallelogram ABCD, the length of the line joining the midpoints of AD and AC is 2 units. If the perimeter of the parallelogram is 26 units, then find the length of AD.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Let **M** and **N** be the midpoints of **AD** and **AC** in **ΔADC**.

By the **Midpoint Theorem**, the line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to and half the length of the third side.

⇒ MN = CD ÷ 2

⇒ 2 = CD ÷ 2 ⇒ CD = 4 units

⇒ Opposite side AB = CD = 4 units

Perimeter = 2 × (AD + CD) ⇒ 26 = 2 × (AD + 4) ⇒ AD + 4 = 13 ⇒ AD = 9 units

**∴ The correct answer is 9 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of parallelogram ABCD = 26 units

Length of the line joining midpoints of **AD** and **AC** = 2 units

**Formula Used:**

Midpoint Theorem in a triangle: MN = 1/2 × third side

Perimeter of a parallelogram = 2 × (Sum of adjacent sides)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca94e87f590c4057c61e6fe960dc4ed4218c3c1311ef15524a74f52f1e14948c.png] 
**Calculations:**

Consider **ΔADC** inside the parallelogram ABCD.

Let **M** be the midpoint of **AD** and **N** be the midpoint of **AC**.

⇒ MN = 2 units

Applying Midpoint Theorem in **ΔADC**:

⇒ MN = CD ÷ 2

⇒ 2 = CD ÷ 2

⇒ CD = 4 units

Since opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal:

⇒ AB = CD = 4 units

Now, let the length of **AD** be x units.

Perimeter of ABCD = 2 × (AD + CD)

⇒ 26 = 2 × (x + 4)

⇒ 13 = x + 4

⇒ x = 9 units

⇒ AD = 9 units

**∴ The correct answer is 9 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Midpoint Theorem

The line segment connecting the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and is exactly half the length of that third side.

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are parallel and equal in length. Opposite angles are equal, and adjacent angles are supplementary (sum to 180°).</p

questions.question: The HCF of 16, 20 and 24 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**HCF** is the **highest common factor** that divides all given numbers exactly.

Calculate differences between numbers: 20 − 16 = **4** and 24 − 20 = **4**.

Since 4 divides 16 (4×4), 20 (4×5), and 24 (4×6), it is the HCF.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 16, 20, and 24.

**Method:** **Prime Factorization Method**

⇒ Prime factors of 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁴

⇒ Prime factors of 20 = 2 × 2 × 5 = 2² × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3

⇒ Common prime factors = 2 × 2

⇒ HCF = 2² = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The greatest number which divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. Also known as **GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)**.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest number which is a multiple of two or more numbers. For 16, 20, 24, the LCM is 240.

Relationship Formula

For two numbers a and b: **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**.</p

The empirical relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

Rearranging this: Mode − Median = 2 Median − 2 Mean.

Factoring out 2: Mode − Median = 2 (Median − Mean).

This matches expression 1 exactly.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

⇒ Simplify the right side: Mode − Median = 2 Median − 2 Mean

⇒ Factor out 2: Mode − Median = 2 (Median − Mean)

⇒ This confirms expression 1 is correct.

⇒ Checking expression 3: Mode = 2 Median − Mean (Incorrect, should be 3 Median − 2 Mean).

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

questions.question: Which of the following factors decreases the rate of evaporation?

__
 
• **Humidity** is the amount of water vapor present in the air. When humidity increases, the air becomes more saturated with water vapor, reducing the rate of evaporation.
 
• As the air becomes more saturated with moisture, the difference between the vapor pressure of the water and the air decreases, which slows down the evaporation process.
 
• High humidity levels mean that the air is close to being fully saturated with water vapor, leaving less room for additional water molecules to evaporate.
 
• Increased humidity directly affects the rate of evaporation because evaporation requires the removal of water vapor from the evaporating surface to the air.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaporation:** It is the process by which water changes from a liquid to a gas or vapor. Evaporation is a crucial part of the water cycle.
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:** Key factors that affect the rate of evaporation include temperature, surface area, wind speed, and humidity.
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures provide more energy to water molecules, increasing the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Wind Speed:** Increased wind speed removes the water vapor from the surface, enhancing the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Surface Area:** A larger surface area allows more water molecules to escape, increasing the rate of evaporation.

questions.question: Which tissue is a distinctive feature of complex plants, one that has made possible their survival in the terrestrial environment?

• **Epithelial tissue**: Also found in animals, it forms the covering or lining of all internal and external body surfaces.
 
• **Tracheophytes**: These are vascular plants that have developed specialized vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) for conducting water and nutrients.
 
• **Primary and secondary growth**: Primary growth increases the length of the plant, while secondary growth increases the girth, both facilitated by vascular tissue.

questions.question: There are two sections A and B of a class, consisting of 18 and 22 students, respectively. If the average weight of section A is 40 kg and that of section B is 35 kg, find the average weight of the whole class.
questions.solution:

Ratio of students in **Section A** and **Section B** = 18 : 22 = 9 : 11.

Using **weighted average** formula: Average = (9 × 40 + 11 × 35) ÷ (9 + 11)

Average = (360 + 385) ÷ 20 = 745 ÷ 20 = 37.25 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 37.25 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0313076a3d3a2ad1d6a02c550d0cd78d860bead964ca1bca0638dbd93aa752c9.png] 

**Given:**

Students in **Section A** (n₁) = 18, Average weight (w₁) = 40 kg

Students in **Section B** (n₂) = 22, Average weight (w₂) = 35 kg

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

⇒ Total weight of **Section A** = 18 × 40 = 720 kg

⇒ Total weight of **Section B** = 22 × 35 = 770 kg

⇒ Total weight of the whole class = 720 + 770 = 1490 kg

⇒ Total number of students = 18 + 22 = 40

⇒ Average weight of the whole class = 1490 ÷ 40 = 37.25 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37.25 kg.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a common drawback of using soap in hard water?

• Hard water contains high concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions.
 
• When soap is used in hard water, it reacts with these ions to form an insoluble precipitate called soap scum.
 
• This soap scum reduces the effectiveness of soap, making it less efficient for cleaning purposes.
 
• Soap scum can accumulate on surfaces, making them difficult to clean and potentially causing damage over time.
 
• The formation of soap scum is a common issue in areas with hard water and requires special detergents or water softeners to mitigate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Water Softening:**

• Common methods include ion-exchange resins and the use of water softening agents.
 
 
 
• **Soap:**
 
 
• Made from the reaction of fats and oils with an alkali, such as sodium hydroxide.
 
• Effective in soft water but forms scum in hard water.
 
 
 
• **Detergents:**
 
 
• Synthetic cleaning agents that are more effective in hard water compared to traditional soaps.
 
• Contain compounds that do not form scum with calcium and magnesium ions.

questions.question: The work done (in Joule) by a constant force of 10 N on an object that is displaced by an amount D meter in the direction of the force is:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work** is defined as the product of the force applied to an object and the displacement of the object in the direction of the force.
 
• The formula for work done by a constant force is given by **W = F × D**, where W is the work, F is the force, and D is the displacement.
 
• Given that the force (F) is 10 N and the displacement (D) is in the direction of the force, the work done can be calculated as **W = 10 × D**.
 
• Therefore, the work done by a constant force of 10 N on an object that is displaced by D meters in the direction of the force is **+10D Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule (J)**:

 
 
• The unit of work in the International System of Units (SI) is the Joule (J).
 
• 1 Joule is defined as the amount of work done when a force of 1 Newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Force (N)**:
 
 
• The unit of force in the International System of Units (SI) is the Newton (N).
 
• 1 Newton is defined as the force required to accelerate a mass of 1 kilogram at a rate of 1 meter per second squared.
 
 
 
• **Displacement**:
 
 
• Displacement is a vector quantity that refers to the change in position of an object.
 
• It is measured in meters (m) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Principle**:
 
 
• The work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• This principle is fundamental in understanding the relationship between force, work, and energy.

questions.question: Which technique is useful for the separation of colloidal particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centrifugation technique**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Centrifugation** is a technique used to separate colloidal particles based on their size, shape, and density.
 
• During centrifugation, a mixture is spun at high speeds, causing denser particles to move outward to the bottom of the tube while lighter particles remain closer to the center.
 
• This method is particularly effective in separating particles that are too small to be filtered out by conventional filtration methods.
 
• Centrifugation is widely used in laboratories and industrial processes to isolate and purify biological molecules, cells, and sub-cellular components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation**: A technique where a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid phase, typically used for purifying substances.
 
• **Filtration**: A method that separates solid particles from liquids or gases using a filter medium that allows the fluid to pass through but not the solid particles.
 
• **Recrystallization**: A technique used to purify chemicals by dissolving both impurities and a compound in an appropriate solvent, then allowing the compound to crystallize out.
 
• **Colloids**: These are mixtures where very small particles of one substance are evenly distributed throughout another without settling out or separating.
 
• **Applications of Centrifugation**: It is used in various fields including biochemistry, molecular biology, and medicine, for purposes like blood separation, DNA/RNA extraction, and purification of proteins.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true with respect to regeneration?

options.text: No organism on earth has the ability to regenerate.
Regeneration and reproduction are the same process with different names in all organisms.
Regeneration gives rise to a totally new organism.
Regeneration is not the same as reproduction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regeneration is not the same as reproduction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regeneration is a biological process where organisms replace or restore lost or damaged tissues, organs, or body parts.
 
• While some organisms can regenerate parts of their bodies, this process does not always result in the creation of a new organism.
 
• Regeneration is distinct from reproduction, which involves the creation of a new organism from one or two parent organisms.
 
• Examples of organisms with high regenerative capabilities include starfish, planarians, and certain species of lizards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planarians:** Flatworms known for their remarkable regenerative abilities, capable of regrowing entire bodies from small segments.
 
• **Autotomy:** A defense mechanism in some animals, such as lizards, where they shed a body part (e.g., tail) to escape predators, which can later regenerate.
 
• **Stem Cells:** Undifferentiated cells that play a critical role in the regeneration process by differentiating into various cell types to replace damaged tissues.
 
• **Asexual Reproduction:** A mode of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes, resulting in offspring genetically identical to the parent, distinct from regeneration.
 
• **Epimorphosis:** A type of regeneration where cells proliferate at the site of injury and differentiate to form new tissues, commonly seen in amphibians.

questions.question: Suppose a number of rays parallel to the principal axis are falling on a concave mirror, then all the reflected rays will intersect:

• When parallel rays of light fall on a concave mirror, they reflect and meet at a single point known as the principal focus.
 
• This phenomenon occurs due to the converging nature of a concave mirror.
 
• The distance from the mirror's surface to this focal point is called the focal length.
 
• The principal focus is located on the principal axis of the mirror, halfway between the mirror's surface and its center of curvature.
 
• This property of concave mirrors makes them useful in applications such as telescopes, headlights, and solar furnaces.

• Focal length is the distance between the pole of the mirror and the principal focus.
 
• It is denoted by the letter 'f' and is a crucial parameter in determining the mirror's reflective properties.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature**
 
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere from which the concave mirror is a part.

questions.question: A large tanker can be filled by two pipes A and B in 60 minutes and 40 minutes, respectively. How many minutes will it take to fill the tanker from empty state, if B is used for half the time and A and B fill it together for the other half?&
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work** (tank capacity) = LCM(60, 40) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 units/min; Efficiency of B = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/min.

In first half-time (T/2), only B works → Work = 3 × (T/2).

In second half-time (T/2), A and B work together → Work = (2 + 3) × (T/2) = 5 × (T/2).

Total work = 1.5T + 2.5T = 4T = 120 ⇒ T = 30 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

 Pipe A
 60
 120 units
 2

 Pipe B
 40
 3

**Given:** Total time taken is **T** minutes.

**Formula:** Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Work done by B in first half = 3 × (T/2)

⇒ Work done by A + B in second half = (2 + 3) × (T/2) = 5 × (T/2)

⇒ Total Work = (3T/2) + (5T/2) = 8T/2 = 4T

⇒ 4T = 120

⇒ T = 120 ÷ 4

⇒ T = 30 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 30 min.**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If a pipe fills a tank in 'x' hours, its 1-hour work is 1/x.

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' and pipe B fills in 'y', time together is (x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

questions.question: An object of height 30 cm is placed in front of a concave lens and an image of height 10 cm is formed. The magnification of the lens is:

questions.question: A constant force is acting on a body of mass 2 kg for 4 s and its velocity changes from 8 m/s to 12 m/s. The magnitude of the applied force is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• States that the **force** acting on an object is equal to the **mass** of the object multiplied by its **acceleration**, represented as **F = m × a**.
 
• This principle explains how the velocity of an object changes when subjected to an external force.
 
 
 
• The mass (**m**) of the body is given as **2 kg** in the question.
 
• The velocity of the body changes from **8 m/s** to **12 m/s**.
 
 
• The change in velocity (**Δv**) can be calculated as: **Δv = final velocity - initial velocity = 12 m/s - 8 m/s = 4 m/s**.
 
 
 
• The time (**t**) over which this change occurs is given as **4 seconds**.
 
 
• Using the formula for acceleration (**a = Δv/t**): **a = 4 m/s ÷ 4 s = 1 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• To calculate the magnitude of the force, apply the formula **F = m × a**:
 
 
• Here, **m = 2 kg** and **a = 1 m/s²**.
 
• Therefore, **F = 2 kg × 1 m/s² = 2 N**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1: 2 N**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Second Law:**

 
 
• It establishes the relationship between an object’s mass, acceleration, and the force applied to it.
 
• The unit of force in the **SI system** is the **Newton (N)**, defined as the force required to accelerate a 1 kg mass by 1 m/s².
 
• This law is often used to calculate the acceleration of objects in motion when a force is applied.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• Defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Acceleration is calculated using the formula: **a = Δv/t**, where **Δv** is the change in velocity and **t** is the time taken.
 
 
 
• **Force:**
 
 
• Force is a vector quantity that can change the motion of an object.
 
• It is calculated using the formula: **F = m × a**, where **m** is the mass and **a** is the acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Velocity:**
 
 
• Velocity is a vector quantity that represents the rate of change of an object’s position.
 
• It includes both speed and direction, distinguishing it from scalar quantities like speed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SI Units:**

 
 
• The **Newton** (N) is the standard unit of force in physics.
 
• One Newton is equivalent to **1 kg·m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Application of Newton’s Laws:**
 
 
• Used widely in engineering, mechanics, and physics to understand the motion of objects.
 
• Examples include calculating the forces acting on vehicles, spacecraft, and falling objects.

questions.question: P, Q and R can fill a tank in 9 hours, 18 hours and 12 hours, respectively. They start the work i.e. filling the tank, with P working on hour 1, Q working on hour 2 and R working on hour 3, and then continuing with this cycle till the work is completed. How many hours will be needed to complete this work in this manner?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** (LCM of 9, 18, 12) = **36 units**.

**Efficiencies:** P = 4, Q = 2, R = 3. Total for 1 cycle (3 hours) = 4 + 2 + 3 = **9 units**.

Number of cycles = 36 ÷ 9 = **4 cycles**.

Total time = 4 cycles × 3 hours/cycle = **12 hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 **Person** **Hours** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 P 9 36 4 
 Q 18 2 
 R 12 3 

**Step-by-step calculation:**

⇒ Work done in **Hour 1** (P) = 4 units

⇒ Work done in **Hour 2** (Q) = 2 units

⇒ Work done in **Hour 3** (R) = 3 units

⇒ Total work in **1 cycle** (3 hours) = 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 units

⇒ Total time required = (Total Work ÷ Work per cycle) × Time per cycle

⇒ Total time = (36 ÷ 9) × 3

⇒ Total time = 4 × 3 = 12 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Work Pattern

In alternate work problems, calculate the work done in one complete **cycle** first. Total time = (Full cycles × items in cycle) + (remaining work ÷ next person's efficiency).

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to the **time taken** to complete the work. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

questions.question: When a decomposition reaction of Limestone is carried out by heating, it is called

__
 
• **Thermal decomposition** is a chemical reaction where a compound breaks down into two or more products when heated.
 
• Limestone (CaCO₃) undergoes thermal decomposition to produce calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).

questions.question: Two trains, 125 m and 165 m in length, respectively, are running in opposite directions, one at the rate of 80 km/h and the other at the rate of 65 km/h. In how many seconds will they be completely clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Relative Speed** in opposite direction = 80 + 65 = 145 km/h.

Convert km/h to m/s: 145 × (5/18) m/s.

**Total Distance** = 125 + 165 = 290 m.

Time = 290 ÷ [145 × (5/18)] = (290 × 18) ÷ (145 × 5) = 2 × 18 ÷ 5 = 36 ÷ 5 = 7.2 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2878d5e6122b93726503819fc5cf911f8001377c24f720592ede54f27154f5b9.png] 
**Given:**

Length of **Train 1** (L₁) = 125 m

Length of **Train 2** (L₂) = 165 m

Speed of **Train 1** (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of **Train 2** (S₂) = 65 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 125 + 165 = 290 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 80 + 65 = 145 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 145 × (5/18) = 725/18 m/s

⇒ Time = 290 ÷ (725/18)

⇒ Time = (290 × 18) ÷ 725

⇒ Time = 5220 ÷ 725 = 7.2 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Rules

When moving in **opposite directions**, speeds are added (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the **same direction**, speeds are subtracted (S₁ − S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses another train, the **total distance** traveled is the sum of the lengths of both trains.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is the rod-shaped structure found in the nucleus only when the cell is about to divide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chromosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chromosomes are rod-shaped structures that become visible during cell division.
 
• They are composed of DNA and proteins and carry genetic information.
 
• Chromosomes ensure that DNA is accurately replicated and distributed during cell division.
 
• Each species has a characteristic number of chromosomes; for humans, it's 46.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chromatin:**

 
 
• Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein found in the nucleus, which condenses to form chromosomes during cell division.
 
• In its uncondensed form, chromatin is involved in gene expression and DNA replication.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:**
 
 
• Mitosis is the process of cell division that results in two daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It involves stages such as prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
 
 
 
• **Meiosis:**
 
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell.
 
• It is essential for sexual reproduction and genetic diversity.
 
 
 
• **Genome:**
 
 
• The genome is the complete set of genes or genetic material present in a cell or organism.
 
• In humans, the genome is organized into 23 pairs of chromosomes.

questions.question: If the price of rice is 30% less than that of wheat, then the price of wheat is approximately what percentage more than that of rice?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If one value is **R% less** than another, then the second value is **more** than the first by: [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100.

Substitute R = 30: [30 ÷ (100 − 30)] × 100

⇒ (30 ÷ 70) × 100 = 300 ÷ 7

⇒ 42.857...% ≈ 42.86%

**∴ The correct answer is 42.86%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The price of **rice** is 30% less than **wheat**.

**Formula Used:**

Percentage More = [(Difference) ÷ (Lower Value)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/905cc76748aa0514eb3dcb356742706101bc5708cf5342fc5de9acd91c554e1b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the price of **wheat** = ₹100

⇒ Price of **rice** = 100 − 30% of 100 = ₹70

⇒ Difference in price = 100 − 70 = ₹30

⇒ Percentage more = (30 ÷ 70) × 100

⇒ Percentage more = 3/7 × 100

⇒ Percentage more = 42.8571% ≈ 42.86%

**∴ The correct answer is 42.86%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Base Value Rule

In percentage comparison, the value following **than** or **of** is usually taken as the denominator (base value).

Fractional Equivalents

Memorizing 1/7 = 14.28% helps solve quickly. Thus, 3/7 = 3 × 14.28% = 42.84%, which rounds to 42.86%.

Percentage Increase vs. Decrease

If A is R% more than B, then B is [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100 % less than A.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the principal axis of a spherical mirror?

options.text: It is parallel to the surface of the mirror.
It intersects the surface of the mirror at an angle of 45 degrees.
It is located at the edge of the mirror.
It is normal to the mirror at its pole.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is normal to the mirror at its pole.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The principal axis of a spherical mirror is a straight line that passes through the center of curvature and the pole of the mirror.
 
• It is normal (perpendicular) to the surface of the mirror at the pole (the geometric center of the mirror's surface).
 
• The principal axis is used as a reference line for drawing ray diagrams and for defining various points related to the mirror, such as the focal point and the center of curvature.
 
• The principal axis helps in understanding the image formation by concave and convex mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pole (P)**: The pole is the midpoint of the spherical mirror's surface. It is the point where the principal axis meets the mirror.
 
• **Center of Curvature (C)**: The center of curvature is the center of the sphere from which the spherical mirror is a part. It lies on the principal axis.
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R)**: The radius of curvature is the distance between the pole and the center of curvature. It is equal to the radius of the sphere from which the mirror is made.
 
• **Focal Point (F)**: The focal point is the point on the principal axis where parallel rays of light either converge (concave mirror) or appear to diverge (convex mirror) after reflection. It is located at half the distance between the pole and the center of curvature.
 
• **Focal Length (f)**: The focal length is the distance between the pole and the focal point. It is given by the formula f = R/2, where R is the radius of curvature.

questions.question: Which of the following plant cells have large membranous organelles that help in photosynthesis?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plastids** are large membranous organelles found in plant cells and some algae.
 
• They are primarily responsible for **photosynthesis**, which is the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Plastids contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which is essential for capturing light energy.
 
• They also play a role in the synthesis and storage of food by the plant.
 
• Plastids can differentiate into various forms, such as **chloroplasts, chromoplasts,** and **leucoplasts**, depending on their function and the needs of the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts:** A type of plastid that contains chlorophyll and is the site of photosynthesis in plant cells.
 
• **Chromoplasts:** Plastids responsible for pigment synthesis and storage, giving colors to fruits and flowers.
 
• **Leucoplasts:** Non-pigmented plastids involved in the synthesis and storage of starch, oils, and proteins.
 
• **Thylakoids:** Membranous structures within chloroplasts where the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place.
 
• **Stroma:** The fluid-filled space surrounding thylakoids in chloroplasts, where the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) occurs.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of a plant does NOT take part in vegetative propagation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flower**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction in plants where new plants grow from parts other than seeds.
 
• Roots, stems, and leaves can all give rise to new plants through vegetative propagation.
 
• Common examples include the propagation of plants like potatoes from tubers (stem), onions from bulbs (stem), and Bryophyllum from leaves.
 
• Flowers, however, are primarily involved in sexual reproduction and do not participate in vegetative propagation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vegetative Propagation Methods:**

 
 
• **Cutting:** Involves rooting a severed piece of the parent plant.
 
• **Layering:** Involves bending a stem to the ground and covering it with soil to encourage roots to form.
 
• **Grafting:** Involves joining two plant parts from different plants.
 
• **Tissue Culture:** Growing plants from cells in a nutrient medium.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Ensures uniformity in plant characteristics.
 
• Faster growth and maturity compared to seed propagation.
 
• Preserves desirable traits of the parent plant.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Lack of genetic diversity, making plants susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• Propagation materials may carry diseases.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Vegetatively Propagated Plants:**
 
 
• Potato (tubers), Sweet Potato (roots).
 
• Strawberry (runners), Sugarcane (stem cuttings).
 
• Bryophyllum (leaves), Onion (bulbs).

questions.question: The temperature at which a liquid starts boiling at atmospheric pressure is known as
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**boiling point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid changes to a gas at atmospheric pressure.
 
• At the boiling point, the vapor pressure of the liquid equals the external pressure surrounding the liquid.
 
• The boiling point of water at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere) is 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• Different liquids have different boiling points depending on their molecular structure and intermolecular forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Triple Point:**

 
 
• The triple point is the temperature and pressure at which three phases (gas, liquid, and solid) of a substance coexist in thermodynamic equilibrium.
 
• For water, the triple point occurs at 0.01 degrees Celsius and 611.657 pascals.
 
 
 
• **Fusion Point:**
 
 
• The fusion point, also known as the melting point, is the temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid.
 
• For water, this occurs at 0 degrees Celsius (32 degrees Fahrenheit) under standard atmospheric pressure.
 
 
 
• **Melting Point:**
 
 
• The melting point is the temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid.
 
• Melting point and fusion point are often used interchangeably.
 
 
 
• **Vapor Pressure:**
 
 
• Vapor pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapor in equilibrium with its liquid or solid phase.
 
• The vapor pressure increases with temperature until it equals the external pressure, leading to boiling.
